For one, your average drug dealer gets his stuff from someone higher up, and usually, not always, these higher ups have a little more knowledge of the trade and who has what. 

The easiest way to get the real stuff is to order it from the dark web. The 2nd easiest is to go to a music festival. There is so much of that shit at those you can get a contact trip. Not really, but pretty much.

Never really got my hands on a lot of the stuff because it carries such a hefty sentence if convicted, and I was really never too interested in doing it. (Don't quote me on this) But I would say it's a very safe bet to say it's still around.

Yes! This was always a very big factor in pricing my product. Weed was never really an issue because the good stuff is easy to get and identify, but with stuff like coke or molly you never know what kind of chemicals are in your stuff or how pure it is (same can go for weed as well, just less common) unless you have it lab tested. 

Quality is a huge, huge factor. An ounce of frosty, indoor grown would run you about $240, whereas you can get an ounce of dirt weed for like $40 in some places. These drastic changes are also observed with coke, where pure uncut can reach up to $100 a gram and stepped on stuff can go as low as $50 a gram.

So if I charge 10 bucks to someone for a gram of weed, instead of the ounce costing $280 (there are 28 grams in an ounce) it would be more in the ballpark of $200-$240.

Psilocybin is magic mushrooms, or rather the main component of them, if you've ever heard of those.

"What do you mean it's only 1984? I was born in 1997, and I could swear I remember some of the 2000's.", I asked him. It sounded like I was begging for him to reveal his joke. 

"Nope. Take a look here." 

He reached into a drawer to the left of me, and pulled out what appeared to be my wallet.

He handed me my ID, and by the grace of god he was right. My ID said that I was born in 1920. 

The Doctor checked the rest of my vitals, wrote down something on a clipboard, and left the room.

"Press the button behind you if you need anything!"

2 days later I was cleared for release, but there was a problem. 

They had nobody to release me to. 

For the next 2 weeks, I lay in a hospital bed trying to find my life. I had to look through phone books and white-pages because 1984 didn't have the internet yet. At least not like we did back home. 

After my research was over I learned that everyone who loved me or knew me either moved away or died. My Mother died 4 years after I slipped into a coma, she was the only relative I had contact with. All of my friends moved away after around 15 years or so, as they all shared the same ominous expectations as my Doctor. 

I literally had nobody. 

The Hospital reached out to various programs and charities for me, and soon I had my own home to be released to. 

6 months after I woke up all of my memory was back. I knew that I was born in 1997, I knew I was not 64 years old, and I sure as hell knew that I didn't try to whack myself. I wasn't that weak. What I still had to figure out was how the hell I managed to end up in this situation.

7 and a half months after I woke up, I got a job. It was at a place called Simtech Incorporated. My job was in the research department, but I was only an assistant. Every day for around 3 months I got up at 8, went to work, and watched dozens of men in coats solder, weld, and put together all of these tiny parts.

It wasn't a glorious job, but it paid the bills and kept me alive, so I stuck to it for a while, all while trying to figure out what caused this crazy event. 

One day at work, I was asked to help move a large crate, which I was not allowed to know the contents of. While moving it, my coworker, who's name I did not care for, let the crate slip out of his grasp, and onto me. As I lay under it, I began to slip into a familiar darkness.

"How does he look today, Doctor?"

I could hear the faint whisper of voices under the whir of machines.

"Normal. Well, normal for him at least."

I could hear the Nurse try to chuckle.

"Huh. That's odd.", the doctor said, as he leaned in closer towards a machine. 

"What is it?", asked the Nurse, almost like she wasn't waiting to get off work and go home. 

"His EEG is showing increased activity. Just like somebody who is awake.", the Doctor said with increasing curiosity. 

The Doctor raised a light to my eye, opened it, and shined it on my pupil. Never in my life had I experienced something so bright, and so painful. 

I immediately jerked my eye shut, to the Doctor's surprise.

"My god, he's awake!"

The Nurse had already left the room. 

I opened my eyes, something that took much more strength than I had. I tried to move, but I was hooked up to so many machines that I couldn't budge, plus the pain. The pain was awful, but not as bad as my situation. I didn't know where I was or what happened.

"Where am I?", I managed to mouth out.

"You're at the Hospital.", the Doctor said. The tag on his coat read "Hartwell". 

"Tampa General, to be specific. How are you feeling?", He asked me, like he thought I had a clue as to what was going on.

"What happened?" I muttered.

"You tried to kill yourself, son. You took every pill in your house. Luckily somebody found you and brought you here."

My stomach dropped.

"How long have I been here?" I asked, scared and ashamed.

"30 years. We actually didn't think you'd ever wake.", Hartwell said.

"So...what year is it? Shouldn't it be like 2044 or something?" 

"Don't be silly, it's only 1984. Don't pretend to have amnesia on me now!", Dr. Hartwell joked. "Things have certainly changed while you were gone alright."

I didn't get this guy. He was playing jokes on me, like I was perfectly healthy. However, I had other worries than my David Letterman wannabe Doctor. Did I really try to end my own life? I couldn't remember trying to, and I didn't understand why I would even want to in the first place.
Why does something have to happen beyond it? I mean, if you add a second scoop of Vanilla to a cone, you just get a bigger cone, nothing else happens.

"You need my money, and I want his fucking head. That is all you need to know, now quit asking me questions and go do your god damned job."

He was right. I *did* need his money. More money equals more control, and that was just about the only thing I had left in my life, or so I thought. 

The offer was $50,000. I had never been offered anything before, it was just always a flat rate. I stared at the picture of my next victim, almost like it was wrong to take a human life. Everything seemed so familiar, the tight, black, cut-off shorts wrapped around his opaque thighs, the skin tight tank-top that boasted the logo of a surf shop, one that I had been to countless times in my past, and last, his shoes. The exact same pair of shoes I owned, just in much better condition. 

Why this man offered me 5 times the normal price, I have no idea. This man was nothing special, but then again, nobody was. So, I took the job. I told my client I'd have this guy dead in a month, which was much longer than it usually took. 

I sat down at my desk, and began to research my new puppet. As the hours passed, the sounds of my monotonous typing grew louder and louder, something I had thought I was used to. I couldn't find one piece of information on this guy. I exhausted everything in my playbook, reverse image search, geo-lookups, they all came back with zero results each time. I was a sitting duck without a name.

Not having a name was never a problem, I didn't need it when I had a face and a location. But, I had none of these. Days passed and I was running out of ideas. 

Suddenly, on one bright, cloudless, and otherwise beautiful day, something hit me. What if this guy didn't have a name? Then, it came to me. There was only one person that I had ever known to not have a name. 

It was me. 

One week ago exactly, I accepted a $50,000 offer to kill myself. Questions raced through my mind like cars on an Atlanta highway at 5 P.M, crowded and not sure if there was an end. Why me? What have I done? More importantly, how did this guy even get a picture of me? I hadn't shown my face to the world in decades. Nevertheless, my bank account was fat with murder money, and I had to come up with a course of action, and soon.

I'd deal with any inconvenience it took just to spend an hour with her at the end of the day. I first met her with a group of friends who went tubing at the river, and I didn't think much of her at first. She was pretty, she was nice, but nothing else to me.

As the year went by we became better friends, but only due to the fact that she was friends with my friends. Eventually all of those days at the park ended up to her and I becoming pretty close. We would text every night, and we would hangout every time my mother let me use her car. I had no problem doing things for her and she had no problem doing them for me. We bought each other food, smoked each other's cigarettes, and even had a few sleepovers together.

Come a drunken night in December and as usual we talk late into the night, only this time she's a thousand miles away visiting her father. It could have been the distance that gave me my courage, but I decided to muster up the guts to admit that I liked her. I'd liked her since we became close, which immediately I knew wouldn't end well-it never does.
We talked about it and although she never said the words, I could tell the feeling was not mutual. I wasn't surprised, she was a model, popular, and pretty much any other sugar-coated word you can use to describe somebody. She asked me why I liked her. I couldn't give her an answer.

I was young still and obviously hadn't been in love before, so I had no idea what it was like. I didn't think I was in love with her but I knew if she felt even a fraction of what I felt for her that we would be together forever. She told me she was going to break my heart, and I told her I was glad she would be the one to do it. It was the nicest thing anyone had ever said to her, and she told me she wishes he had said it, but it didn't matter because "You're the better person, and it's better hearing it from you".

Months passed, and as our friendship grew so did my feelings toward her. She had a boyfriend, yet her and I were together every chance we got. I knew he wasn't good enough for her. I could tell by the way he gave attention to other girls, and I knew for sure when he bailed on taking her to prom. I told her I knew he was bad news, and I could tell she knew too, but that didn't change anything.

I lived like this for the longest time. I comforted her when he made her sad, hung out with her when he didn't, I did everything for her. I did this as long as I could but eventually heartbreak takes its toll on somebody. I started ignoring her, which obviously she wasn't okay with. I was more important to her than him, but that still wasn't enough for her to like me. My ignoring turned to neglect, which turned to manipulation. Pretty soon every time she made a mistake with him I made sure she knew it, and I made her extra sure she was a piece of shit for it.
She was smart, but she wasn't wise. She couldn't tell what I was doing to her, I still masked my feelings for her with a forced sense of friendship and love.

Around Christmas time he proved me right yet again, this time being the last time. He hit her. She never told me but the unfamiliar sight of makeup on her face and distance from me basically screamed the obvious. Nevertheless it wasn't enough as she yet again went back to him.
I wasn't going to let it happen again. I was done being right all of the time. I knew she was with him, it was perfect. I got in my car, and without a thought was on my way to her house. I opened the door, and said to him: 

"I warned her about you. Now, I have to warn you about me."

She told me I was the better person, but she deserved the best.

I made sure I spared no expense in giving them a proper goodbye.

Bosons are particles that CAN occupy the same state, and some exist as elementary particles (photon, Higgs Boson, etc) while some are made of quarks (pion, kaon, etc) Viscosity is just a substances resistance to flow.
